entries.note: The forecast is hedged ('I think... might') and hyperbolic. The $4.65 trillion exposure figure inside it could be checked on its own.

entries.test: Whether each major GPU/TPU buyer other than Microsoft (e.g. Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle, CoreWeave) raises tens of billions of dollars in debt to fund its AI hardware purchases.
entries.note: No deadline is given. Some buyers may have already issued large bonds.

entries.test: Market reporting on why CoreWeave's debt sold off and why AI data center debt markets cooled, plus the UBS estimate of about $102 billion in debt needs and CoreWeave's disclosed backlog.
entries.note: Attributing a market mood to one cause is contested, but reporting on the selloff gives a shared test.

entries.test: After a major AI data center customer fails to pay, whether other customers also default, demand for AI data centers falls, and resale values of data center assets drop.
entries.note: This is a contagion chain with no deadline.

entries.test: CoreWeave bond yields around October 20, 2026, as shown by market data.
entries.note: Only the yield figure is cleanly checkable. The 'only way to calm investor anxiety' part is his judgment.

entries.test: Amazon's reported capex for the most recent quarter, and Business Insider's reporting on the projected $3 billion a month in GB300 rack deliveries and on racks waiting in warehouses.
entries.note: The $3 billion a month came from a projection in an internal email, but he states it as current fact.

entries.test: Evidence on whether NVIDIA pushed customers to take early GPU delivery, and whether industry analyses tie the rise in RAM and consumer electronics prices to that, rather than to real AI memory demand.
entries.note: This is a contested causal claim, and the 'artificial' framing is the key point to test.
This is a claim about Huang's motive, made inside an insult passage. The 'we did not need' part is a value judgment.

entries.test: Anthropic's disclosed compute cost per megawatt compared with its revenue per megawatt (e.g. in IPO filings).
entries.note: This is arithmetic on Nomura's roughly $20 billion per GW figure, taken as annual cost against annual revenue. It is close to a tautology given that premise.

entries.test: Whether Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Meta disclose AI revenue, and whether published analyst estimates put more than 70% of the hyperscalers' AI revenue on OpenAI and Anthropic.
entries.note: The claim is mainly a report of disclosures and analyst estimates. The 'contingent' part is secondary.

entries.test: Public estimates of global AI compute rental spend outside OpenAI and Anthropic, compared with about $22 billion.
entries.note: This is his own estimate, and the evidence may be limited.
'Services that do not make any economic sense' has no shared measure.

entries.test: AI's share of VC investment in 2025–2026 (e.g. PitchBook/Crunchbase), and VC value creation since 2015 compared with S&P 500 returns.
entries.note: 'Not particularly good at creating value' and 'yet to prove economic worth' are partly judgments.
'Work out' and 'have a problem' have no agreed test.

entries.test: If AI debt markets sour further, whether neoclouds and data center developers pay 12–15% interest on new data center financing.
entries.note: 'Three years in the future' is when the data centers would be built, not the deadline for the forecast. CoreWeave's yields are already near this range.

entries.test: Market reporting on how markets reacted to Anthropic's 47% quarter-over-quarter growth and why, and Anthropic's disclosed non-cancellable compute commitments of about $413 billion.
entries.note: The parts about market psychology ('everybody knows deep down') are softer than the factual parts.
'Cannot bail out' earnings misses or investor sentiment is a rhetorical claim about capability, with no shared test.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI closes its roughly $30 billion round at about a $1.4 trillion valuation.
entries.note: The 'it' that IPOs near $1 trillion is unclear (it could mean OpenAI, not Anthropic). The survival remark expresses uncertainty, not a commitment.
